newsitem.title: FRANCE: European rights court hears Turkey torture case.
newsitem.headline: European rights court hears Turkey torture case.

text.p: Ankara's human rights record came under the spotlight on Wednesday as the European Court of Human Rights heard fresh allegations of torture by the Turkish authorities.
In the latest case to come before the Euro-court, Sukran Aydin of Derik, southeastern Turkey, alleged she was beaten and raped while in the custody of Turkish gendarmes for three days during 1993.
The Turkish government has denied ever detaining Aydin and has countercharged that, according to intelligence reports, she was a terrorist working for the separatist Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK).
A decision was not expected for several months.
The court ruled last month that Turkish police had tortured a Kurd arrested in 1992 as a suspected terrorist but never charged.

In that case, the court ordered Ankara to pay damages and legal costs to the survivors of Zeki Aksoy, who complained he had been tortured while held incomunicado for at least two weeks in a prison in southeastern Turkey.
Turkey had argued in that case, as well, that the allegations were completely unfounded.
The rights court is part of the 40-nation Council of Europe, of which Turkey is a member. The council was set up after World War Two to promote democracy and human rights across Europe.
Aydin, who is now 20 years old, was 16 at the time of her arrest in June 1993. She was never charged.

In a second case involving Turkey, to be heard by the rights court later on Wednesday, four women from the southeastern village of Saggoze allege that Turkish gendarmes burned down 10 to 13 homes in the village in 1993 after PKK guerrillas attacked a gendarme station in nearby Ucdamlar.
They said the gendarmes told them they were burning the houses to punish them for helping terrorists.
Attorneys for the Turkish government have denied official involvement, arguing instead that the houses were burned by members of the PKK who had taken over the village and then fled.
